description: Whole-turn evaluation: did a message in the language Account Managers actually use reach the right capability, identify the right service, and carry the right facts? 'expect' capabilities must all be planned and 'forbid' must not be — but capability assertions only prove the plumbing routes. 'expectItem', 'expectVerdict' and 'expectOutcome' are what test the product: they assert what the resolver actually decided, so a request cannot be answered from the wrong catalogue item and still score green. Assert the item where it is unambiguous, the verdict wherever one should be stated, and the outcome where the correct behaviour is to ask or to name no service at all. Cases marked 'critical' are ones where a wrong answer misleads someone about safety or about money: any failure there fails the run.

cases.knownFailure: Passes in the deployed configuration and fails offline. Telling a genuine second reading of a request from a coincidental shared word is a question about meaning, and keyword scoring cannot answer it: across these cases genuine disagreement measures 0.77-0.99 of the leader's confidence and a pure coincidence 0.79, which no threshold separates. With embeddings the same cases measure 0.88-1.00 against 0.69. Recorded rather than tuned away, because the offline mode is a fallback and asking too often is its safe failure direction.
cases.note: A vague pricing question must not settle on a service. Agreeing on the video items answers 'included, free of charge' to a question about cost.

cases.message: Can we see this month's SEO report?

cases.note: T25 declared '1:1 call' and '121 call' on the two -121 items; 'one to one' would not have worked, because 'one', 'to' and 'on' are all stopwords and that phrasing tokenises to nothing. Reaching the item was never the problem here - admitting a rival alongside it is.
cases.knownFailure:
Asks rather than answers in the deployed configuration, and that is accepted. Four Strategic support items describe calls: the two 121 items are out of scope and the two group items are in scope, so a rival that survives genuinely changes the answer and the resolver is right to ask. It ranks the correct item first every time and says the options are not handled the same way, so nothing is promised. Not gating, because asking is the agreed safe direction when the services named disagree.

Not closed by corpus work, and deliberately not forced. After T27 the leader scores 2.76 against 1.95 and the sales-and-marketing group call drops out of contention entirely, but Monthly marketing catch ups still clears the admission floor by 0.003 on the planner's phrasing. The two retrieval modes want opposite things: pulling this item closer for dense scoring is exactly what put a one-to-one in front of "send us this month's marketing calendar" and cost a turn in the rules eval. A margin of 0.3 percent would flip back on the next model revision, and tuning to it would be tuning to this file.

Settling it belongs to the resolver rather than the corpus. BACKLOG O4 records site-visit as the same shape: a rival admitted close to the leader, where reordering changes nothing because the turn still asks.

cases.message: Can central team schedule our Instagram posts for the week?
cases.note: P0. 'schedule' must reach an item named 'Content scheduling'. The risk is telling an AM that central marketing owns work the DB marks Local, so the reply has to name the local team. It previously banned the substrings 'free of charge' and 'no extra cost' instead, which was wrong: the document says 'Extra cost or quote required: No' and answers its own question with 'No extra cost is required as it is included in the local scope'. A grounded reply quoting its source was failing the assertion. It only ever passed because the deterministic wording is terse; the live composer echoes the document and tripped it on the first nightly run.
